relations.note: Mielikki is Tapio’s wife and co-ruler, holding keys to his game-storehouse.
Tapio can designate the female forest divinity or forest itself, overlapping Mielikki’s identity.
Annikki appears beside Mielikki as they control forest dogs and the bear.
Saint Anne enters forest poetry as Annikki, functioning as a counterpart or substitute for forest women.
Tellervo occupies overlapping wife, daughter, maiden, and attendant roles within Mielikki’s forest household.

relations.myth: Hunt for the Elk of Hiisi
relations.note: Tuulikki drives the elk while Mielikki opens the forest storehouse and releases game.

relations.myth: Hunt for the Elk of Hiisi
relations.note: Nyyrikki clears the hunter’s road while Mielikki is petitioned to release game.
Later systematization presents Nyyrikki as the son of Tapio and Mielikki.
Tyytikki shares animal-driving or bear-restraining duties with Mielikki in variant forest poetry.
Tuometar shares with Mielikki the task of controlling or restraining the bear.
Some bear-origin variants make Mielikki the bear’s mother or progenitress.

relations.myth: Mielikki raises Ohto beneath a spruce
relations.note: Mielikki fosters and raises the bear beneath the flowering crown of a spruce.

relations.myth: The bear receives claws and teeth
relations.note: Mielikki provides the bear claws and teeth after it swears against using them wickedly.
Mielikki restrains the bear, binding its muzzle or dulling its claws near cattle.

relations.myth: Heavenly descent and nurture of the bear
relations.note: Mary sends or handles the bear’s heavenly material before Mielikki nurtures it in the forest.
Mary can replace Mielikki or related female forest guardians in bear and cattle-protection charms.
The air maiden casts material from heaven, after which Mielikki gathers and nurtures the bear.
Väinämöinen invokes Mielikki before hunting the bear and recounts her nurturing of it.

relations.myth: Hunt for the Elk of Hiisi
relations.note: Mielikki is petitioned to open the forest storehouse and release the supernatural elk toward the hunter.
